# Blood Cult
Even in the far future, some things are never quite understood. There are things that lurk in the darkness of space, unspeakable horrors of ancient power that wish to bring ruin to the universe and shape it in their image. They reach out from the void and turn the minds of mortals in their favor, in the hope that one day they will be brought once more into this plane of existence.
The Geometer of Blood, Nar'Sie, has sent a number of her followers to the station. As a cultist you have an abundance of cult magic at your disposal, something for every situation. Work with your brethren to summon an avatar of your eldritch goddess!
The Blood Cult only appears on shifts with at least 15 players.
## Objectives
Every cultist shares two objectives: offer the chosen crew member to Nar'Sie, then summon her.
- 1. Find a discreet spot and contact your allies. Anything you say starting with [bold]:g[/bold] is heard by every cultist, construct and soul shard. - 2. Pick an area to turn into a base: reachable by the cult, but hidden well enough that security won't find it easily. - 3. Draw a teleport rune so every cultist can reach the base. - 4. Draw an empowering rune, then prepare blood spells. Stun spells are your bread and butter, but EMP, Teleport and Blood Rites will make sure you are ready for anything. - 5. Convert new members, or sacrifice the unconvertable, on the rune of offering. Put the soul shards of the sacrificed into construct shells to raise constructs. - 6. Work together to find your sacrifice target, kill them and offer their body. - 7. Prepare to summon Nar'Sie. She can only be summoned where the veil is thin, and the crew will fight desperately to stop you. Make sure you have enough cultists and equipment to hold out. - 8. Gather ten cultists and constructs on the rune of dimensional rending and invoke it.
## The cult reveals itself
The bigger the cult grows, the harder it is to hide.
- At [bold]5[/bold] cultists, every cultist's eyes start glowing red. - At [bold]8[/bold] cultists, every cultist gets a blood halo and Nar'Sie chooses a leader.
## Ritual Dagger
Your dagger is your most important tool:
- Use it in hand to draw runes. Drawing a rune cuts you. - Use it on a rune to erase it. - Use it on a cult barrier to dispel it. - It is also a decent weapon, and can be thrown.
## Runed Metal
Use runed metal in hand to build cult structures:
- [bold]Pylon[/bold]: slowly heals nearby cultists and constructs and turns the floor around it into cult floor. Pylons can't be built close to each other. Click it to turn it on or off. - [bold]Altar[/bold]: makes construct shells and eldritch whetstones. - [bold]Daemon forge[/bold]: makes mirror shields, eldritch longswords, cult armor and flagellant's robes. - [bold]Archives[/bold]: makes cursed orbs, zealot's blindfolds, veil shifters and void torches. - [bold]Runed girder[/bold] and [bold]runed door[/bold]: a second sheet on a girder raises a cult wall.
Each altar, forge and archive has to recharge for a few minutes between uses. The crew can't use cult items: they get knocked down and drop them.
## Minor Runes
These runes can be drawn anywhere on the station.
Converts or sacrifices whoever stands on it. One cultist can sacrifice a corpse, two can convert a living person, and three are needed to sacrifice someone alive who can't be converted (the sacrifice target, the chaplain and anyone with a mindshield). Every offering grants the cult another revival. The souls of the sacrificed end up in soul shards.
Empowers whoever invokes it. While empowered you can hold four spells instead of one, drawing runes is twice as fast and costs half the blood, and preparing spells is twice as fast too. The empowerment fades after a while away from cult floor.
Warps everyone standing on it to another teleport rune. You name the rune when you draw it.
Brings a dead cultist lying on it back to life. The cult starts with three revivals and earns one more with every offering, so use them sparingly.
When invoked, turns into a barrier that blocks passage until it is broken or dispelled with a ritual dagger.
Two cultists can summon any other cultist to the rune, which then fades. Cultists who are cuffed or being dragged can't be summoned.
Three cultists sap their own health to fire bolts of boiling blood at non-believers who can see the rune, setting them alight.
## Final Runes
These runes can only be drawn once the sacrifice target is dead and the cult has at least ten members. They also have to be drawn where the veil is thin; your briefing in the character menu tells you where. Each thin spot can only be used once, so don't waste them all on apocalypse runes or you'll never be able to summon Nar'Sie!
A harbinger of the end times, invoked by three cultists. It sets off a massive EMP, a power grid failure and a solar flare. If the cult makes up less than 15% of the players, it also unleashes one of the following: - Immovable rods (x3) - Mimic vending machines (x2) - A mouse migration (x2) - A meteor swarm (x2) - Spider infestations (x3) - Anomalies (x4) - Kudzu growths (x2)
Tears apart the barriers between worlds to call forth the Geometer. The whole station is told where it was drawn. Ten cultists and constructs have to stand on the rune to invoke it, and the invoker has to hold still for 40 seconds while the crew tries to stop them. If it succeeds, Nar'Sie rises and every cultist becomes a harvester.
## Blood Magic
Blood spells are limited-use magic that fades once spent. Use the [bold]Blood Magic[/bold] action to prepare a spell, or to dispel one you hold. Without an empowering rune, preparing a spell takes longer and you can only hold one at a time. You can't cast blood spells while muted.
- [bold]Stun[/bold]: your hand stuns and mutes the next non-cultist you hit. - [bold]Teleport[/bold]: send yourself or another cultist to a teleport rune. - [bold]Electromagnetic Pulse[/bold]: a large EMP centered on you. - [bold]Shadow Shackles[/bold]: your hand binds and mutes victims. Downed victims are bound at once. Four castings. - [bold]Twisted Construction[/bold]: plasteel becomes runed metal, airlocks become runed doors, and cyborg shells or endoskeletons become construct shells. - [bold]Summon Combat Equipment[/bold]: cult armor, a bola and an eldritch longsword. - [bold]Summon Ritual Dagger[/bold]: in case you lost yours. - [bold]Blood Rites[/bold]: your hand soaks up blood from people, puddles and containers, and spends it to heal cultists and constructs you touch. Use it in hand to forge a blood halberd from 300 units of blood.
A good tip is to always carry a stun and a teleport spell, so you can get out of a risky situation.
## Constructs
Constructs are bound to the cult and must obey their masters. Put a filled soul shard into a construct shell and the soul inside chooses its form. Constructs count as cultists for runes and can hear the cult's mind.
Activating a filled soul shard releases its soul as a shade. Shades are fragile, but activating the shard again pulls them back in. Handy if you need someone to help you activate a rune.
The cult's builder. It can raise cult floors, walls and doors, and summon new soul shards from Nar'Sie's realm.
A fast, clawed assassin. Its phase shift lets it slip through walls unseen for a few seconds; attacking ends it early.
Slow, strong and very tough. It tears through walls, throws up shields and fires a devastating gauntlet echo.
## Fighting the Cult
- The chaplain can't be converted, and can erase runes with their bible and bless soul shards so their constructs serve the crew. - Holy water purges the cult from a cultist after about thirty seconds. Sprayed on a rune, it washes the rune away. - Mindshielded crew can't be converted, only sacrificed by three cultists. - Only cultists can tell what a rune is by examining it.
## Tips
- Always be ready to summon a cultist in trouble. You can't summon them once they're cuffed. - Keeping a shade in a soul shard lets you use two-person runes on your own: release the shade, invoke, recall it. - The EMP spell and the apocalypse rune both open doors for you. Don't forget a crowbar!
